body:
<!-- pr-reviewer: 8c2eec039fd146dea3bcde5d5264c037c4349608 -->
**Needs changes before merge.** One blocker: deleting a plate leaves its fixtures holding a link to it by name, and the next plate that takes that name picks them up.

Reviewed only the two commits on top of #802 (`c2a3f873..8c2eec03`), trial-merged with current `upstream/main` (the merge was clean).

### What looks good
- The plate's collision mesh is a closed 12-triangle solid slab, so the holes are conservative. No new collision code: the plate goes through the existing fixture laws and the posting gate, and `posting` is green.
- Placement works out the pose correctly. `local_pose` puts the fixture on the hole or dowel node at `top_z` and applies the turn (dowel heading + yaw). `stand` puts the mesh's lowest point on the top face, which is valid because only a turn about Z is applied. The pose is composed with the plate's own pose, so a tilted plate carries correctly. `on_the_plate` checks the footprint in the plate's frame.
- Each plate edit is one undo step with an exact inverse. `MoveFixture` carries riders transitively; their before and after poses are snapshotted when the command is created. `SetPlate` regenerates the plate and re-seats the riders in the same step. A move by hand unmounts the fixture in the same step.
- Every refusal is checked when the command is created, and each one says what is wrong: an unknown location, a gap, an off-stagger place, a plate without dowels, overhang (side and amount), placing a fixture on itself, a cycle (walk bounded to 1024 steps), a non-finite turn, and every bad plate figure (including the 20000-hole bound).
- Detection holds up under probing (local, not committed): a hole 0.2 mm off is refused, as are alternating ±0.03 mm jitter and grids turned 0.05°, 0.2°, 1° and 5° in the model frame. A counterbored hole set reads `top_z` as the real top face (0.0), not the counterbore floor.
- Save/load: the `plate` and `on_plate` keys are optional and kept as raw JSON. A key that fails to parse, or a plate that breaks the plate law, is dropped with a log entry and never fails the load (#812). No version bump is needed.
- The MCP tools run the same commands through `History::execute`. The UI adds the menu row, a dialog, the picker and a structural row test.
- No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` outside tests. New `src` modules carry a provenance line. No snapshot PNG changes. No "Saunders", "SMW" or "770 XL" (or Fusion/HSMWorks) in the diff. The 770MX preset is pinned against `tormach-770mx.mch`'s table box. The `Changelog:` line and `Fixes #819` are present, and the commit subjects are conventional.

### Local results (merged with main, macOS, private target)
| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --no-run` | built |
| app `fixture_plate` | 7 passed |
| app `fixture_plate_detect` | 2 passed |
| app `mcp_plate` | 1 passed |
| app `fixture_library` / `builtin_vise` / `mcp_vise` / `fixtures` / `fixture_ux` | 6 / 9 / 1 / 14 / 9 passed |
| app `fixture_mesh` / `fixture_mesh_posed` / `fixture_law_gaps` / `fixture_locate` | 3 / 2 / 3 / 11 passed |
| app `carried_fixtures_cache` / `carried_verify` | 6 / 8 passed |
| app `posting` / `verify` | 17 / 21 passed (2 ignored) |
| app `project_roundtrip` / `commands_undo` / `mcp` | 71 / 32 / 13 passed |
| ui `fixture_plate_tests` / `fixture_library_tests` / `fixture_ux_tests` | 5 / 4 / 6 passed |
| ui `tests::fixture_rows` / `tests::structural` | 4 / 4 passed |
| ui `--lib` (all, CWD `crates/ui`) | 466 passed, 5 ignored |
| ui `trace_parity` (run 3 times) | 5 passed each run |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

On the `trace_parity` SIGSEGV from the Linux batch: it is not related to this PR. That suite exercises `ui::trace` and the sim preview pack over a headless wgpu device, and this PR changes neither. It passed 3 out of 3 runs here as well, so it looks like a headless-GPU flake when run in parallel.

### Requested before merge
1. **A deleted plate's fixtures keep their link to it by name, and the next plate with that name picks them up.** Locations: `crates/app/src/commands/fixture.rs:296-334` (`DeleteFixture`), `crates/app/src/plate/mount.rs` (`riders` matches `mount.plate == name`) and `crates/app/src/commands/insert_fixture.rs:40` (`free_name` hands out a deleted name again).

   Reproduced locally with a probe test:
   1. Insert "Plate 300 x 300 mm" at the origin.
   2. Place `Block` at B2. It lands at (37.5, 37.5, 10).
   3. Delete the plate. `Block` keeps `on_plate = { plate: "Plate 300 x 300 mm", at: B2 }`.
   4. Insert a new 300 mm plate at x = 500. It gets the same name.
   5. `MoveFixture` the new plate by +200 in Y. It reports `carried: ["Block"]`, and `Block` moves to (37.5, 237.5, 10). That fixture was never placed on this plate and is 460 mm away from it.

   After step 4, the row and setup sheet also say `Block` is "at B2" on a plate it isn't on. `SetPlate` on the new plate would move `Block` onto that plate's B2. The collision check still judges the real meshes, so nothing gouges silently. But a command the user did not aim at that fixture moves it, and its recorded location no longer matches its pose. This is the stale-location case the plate laws are meant to rule out.

   Fix: in `DeleteFixture` (and in `ImportFixture` when a re-import drops a plate's grid, `import_fixture.rs:63-70`), clear `plate.mount` on every direct rider in the same command and snapshot it for `invert`. That matches the decision's "deleting a plate leaves its fixtures where they stand", minus the dangling link. Please pin it with a delete → re-insert → move test like the one above. Optionally, on load, drop an `on_plate` whose plate is not in the file, or is not a plate.

### Notes (not blocking)
- **A grid turned exactly 45° in the model frame is accepted, not refused.** The probe read it as a staggered 11×11 lattice with a 17.68 mm pitch and 26 gaps. That is geometrically correct, because a diamond lattice is a checkerboard on X/Y and every named place is a real hole, so placement is safe. But the names won't match the plate's own, and the decision file and PR body say turned grids are refused. Either refuse a stagger whose pitch is far below the hole spacing the user would expect, or document the exception.
- **Detection tolerance.** A hole up to `ON_NODE = 0.05` mm off its node is snapped to the node: 0.04 mm off was accepted in the probe. That is a stated tolerance and fine for workholding, but say it in the dialog/MCP text. The refusal for a slightly turned grid reads "the lattice would hold 3610624 holes", and the one for a single hole 0.2 mm off reads "only 35 of the lattice's 3755 places hold a hole". Both refuse correctly, but neither tells the user what is actually wrong ("turned or irregular"). Also, `Grid::check` doesn't require the pitch to exceed `2 * ON_NODE` or the hole diameter. Once the pitch is under 0.1 mm the on-node test always passes, and only the fill and size bounds stop a bad fit. A `pitch > diameter` guard in `lattice` would make that explicit.
- **The dowel group can be any second lattice.** Four mounting holes of another size at the corners form a 2×2 lattice and become the "dowels". The places are still real holes, so this only affects names.
- **Rider geometry edits aren't re-checked.** Re-importing a rider (`ImportFixture` keeps `mount`) or editing a vise rider's jaws (#802) changes its mesh without re-standing it or re-running the overhang law. The recorded location stays, but the fixture may now float, sink or hang off. The collision check judges the real mesh, so nothing gouges silently, but a re-seat or an unmount there would keep the label honest.
- **`MoveFixture` on a plate only clash-checks the plate.** Its by-name clash warning covers the plate alone, not the riders it carries into a part or the stock. That is a warning, not a refusal, and posting still judges every mesh.
- **File size.** Growth of files already over ~400 lines: `crates/ui/src/state.rs` (+33, 4189 lines), `egui_app/shell.rs` (+10), `egui_app/pages.rs` (+5). `crates/app/tests/fixture_plate.rs` is 402 lines.
- **Provenance.** The new test files carry gate maps but no provenance line. That matches the existing fixture tests, so it's fine either way.
- **"770 XL" in the PR text.** It appears only in the PR body and the issue comment, not in the repo.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
